evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Climatic Requirements' (Vegetable Production series), Table 1

frostTender.notes: Same document also lists okra's optimum/min/max temperature band as '21-29 / 18 / 35' alongside chili, eggplant, sweet potato and watermelon (Table 2, p3), and notes okra seed germinates poorly below 20°C soil temperature and not at all at 10°C ('Okra N N 27 17 13 7 6', Table 3, p4, where N = no germination at 5°C and 10°C).

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Length of Growing Period' (Vegetable Production series), Table 4

transplant.notes: Inferred from the table's own footnote convention: rows for transplanted crops (e.g. Brinjal) are marked with an asterisk ('* denotes time from transplanting', p3) and the Okra row carries no asterisk, implying it is measured from direct sowing. This is an inference from table formatting, not an explicit standalone statement that okra is direct-sown.

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Length of Growing Period' (Vegetable Production series), Table 4

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Corroborated by Starke Ayres' Clemson Spineless cultivar, independently stated as 50-60 days to maturity, an exact match to the KZN DARD figure.

varieties.name: Clemson Spineless
varieties.notes: Described as a moderately ribbed okra with medium-green, straight, spineless pods, recommended for spring and summer planting. Supplier markets it as a general home-garden variety and does not attribute it to a specific South African province or growing zone.

gaps: SowMonths for all four rain patterns (summer, winter, all-year, mild-frost) are unsourced. KZN DARD's own sowing-calendar table (Table 6, 'Plant Establishment') has no Okra row at all — confirmed on both p7 and p8 where the adjoining crops (Brinjal, Cucurbits, Sweet corn) do have rows. No DAFF/DALRRD production brochure for okra could be found: direct nda.gov.za/dalrrd.gov.za access is blocked from this environment, and a rigorous Wayback Machine CDX search (validated first against a known-good match, an existing Eggplant brochure capture, then run as an unfiltered listing of the entire 'Brochures_and_Production_Guidelines' directory, 22 total archived files) found no Okra brochure was ever archived, despite a plausible-looking 'Brochure Okra.pdf' URL appearing in web search results that does not actually resolve.

Row spacing, in-row spacing, sow depth and seed rate are unsourced. KZN DARD's Table 5 (spacing/seed-rate table, 'Plant Establishment', p4-p6) has no Okra row, confirmed by reading the full table twice.
Yield is unsourced. KZN DARD's Table 8 ('Expected Yields', p1-p3) has no Okra row, confirmed by reading the full table.

A South Africa-hosted, peer-reviewed paper on drip-irrigated okra was found on scielo.org.za (Water SA journal, vol. 49 no. 2, 2023, DOI 10.17159/wsa/2023.v49.i2.3990), but on reading its full text it describes an Indian field trial (Haryana Agricultural University, sown in India's June/Kharif season, spacings of 45x40cm or 60x30cm under subsurface drip irrigation) with no connection to South African growing conditions or calendar. It was deliberately excluded as a source for okra spacing or sowMonths, since South Africa's June is a winter/frost month in the interior and using this data would mislead SA farmers despite the source's otherwise-preferred domain.
Only one variety (Clemson Spineless, a general home-garden cultivar) could be verified with a specific maturity figure; no SA commercial/zone-specific okra cultivar guidance was found.
summary: Frost tenderness, days-to-harvest and ECOCROP limits are sourced from KZN DARD's Vegetable Production series and corroborated by Starke Ayres. SowMonths, spacing and yield are all confirmed gaps: no KZN DARD table row exists for okra in any of the sowing-calendar, spacing or yield tables, no DAFF/DALRRD brochure could be located or confirmed to exist (rigorous Wayback CDX search), and the one candidate peer-reviewed source (SciELO, Water SA) was excluded as reporting Indian, not South African, growing conditions.
